messages:
Alex K: heads-up — I'm starting a 30m primary -> secondary handover, saw a couple of p99 spikes earlier, want to flag coverage gaps before I sign off
Tanya: thanks alex. can you share the short list of what you saw and any runbook steps you started?
Alex K: sure — p99 gen latency spiked ~10% for ~8m at 02:12UTC, error rate stayed low, but we saw KV cache miss thrash on a subset of pods. I ran the quick warm restart on two replicas (see cmd below) and ramped down new traffic routing to the older pool
Alex K: ```bash
# warm restart on node group
kubectl rollout restart deploy/gen-worker --namespace=inference --selector=pool=fast
```
Cheng L: noted. did you toggle batching settings or change quant profiles?
Alex K: no config changes. Route policy bumped to fallback-variant for ~2m (automated) — suspect cold KV cache + uneven batching due to bursty prefixes.
Maria S: incident-bot pasted the pager, adding timeline from logs: 
incident-bot: Pager: generation-prod p99_latency > 700ms (alert triggered 2026-03-15T02:12:05Z). Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Suggested runbooks: https://runbooks.redwood.com/kv-cache-thrash, https://runbooks.redwood.com/p99-latency-triage
Samir: ok — if it's KV cache thrash, runbook says try prefix KVCLEAR + gradual restart and temporary priority routing. Link?
Maria S: https://runbooks.redwood.com/kv-cache-thrash (top section has exact steps). quick pointers: 1) increase cache read memo window 2) issue rolling restart on 20% of replicas 3) bump follower read-only capacity if available
Tanya: Alex — are any customers impacted? I saw one support ticket but not widespread.
Alex K: support ticket from ACME Corp reported a slow response in embed generation for a batch job; transient only — I informed support it's mitigated and monitoring. No SLA breach yet.
Cheng L: for handover — who is primary for the next 2 hours? I can stay primary until 04:00UTC, but will be on call for infra as well.
Alex K: thanks. Tanya will be primary after me, Cheng stays as secondary? Tanya: I can take primary until 04:00UTC, Cheng as secondary sounds good. Samir will be on standby for paging escalations.
Tanya: noted. quick checklist for handover: 1) active alerts (none firing now) 2) recent mitigation actions (rolled restart of 2 pods, route fallback) 3) runbooks referenced (KV cache thrash, p99 triage) 4) open customer-ticket ACME-385
Samir: I'll watch the incident-bot timeline, and I'll leave a breakglass note in PagerDuty if anything regresses.
Alex K: leaving a couple of console links and commands in case you need them:
Alex K: - logs: https://logs.redwood.com/generation-prod?from=2026-03-15T02:00
Alex K: - k8s get: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l service=gen-worker -o wide`
Alex K: - rolling restart command I used: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/gen-worker --namespace=inference`
Tanya: before I fully take over — any immediate follow-ups? Should we temporarily increase batching window to smooth bursts?
Cheng L: we can try increasing batching by 50ms on the canary route for 10m, that'll trade a little latency for throughput. If p99 drops, revert.
Samir: do the canary change via console route override: console.redwood.com/routes/gen-prod -> override batching_ms=150 (was 100)
Maria S: logging reminder: tag any mitigation messages with `#handback` and include `first_message_ts` so we can audit later.
Tanya: copying steps into the handoff note and taking primary now. I'll ping if anything pops in 5m. :thumbsup:
Alex K: thanks — leaving the thread. 
incident-bot: Incident closed (automated): p99 alert resolved at 2026-03-15T02:16:30Z. If issues recur, pager will reopen.
Tanya: confirmed no new alerts for 20m. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to Samir if it returns.
Cheng L: thanks all, leaving secondary in place.
Samir: ack, on standby.
Tanya: final quick link dump for next person: runbook KV: https://runbooks.redwood.com/kv-cache-thrash, p99 triage: https://runbooks.redwood.com/p99-latency-triage, emergency rollback: https://runbooks.redwood.com/rollback-guidance
Tanya: handover complete. thread_ts: 1739504321
